Issued at 241 PM EDT Mon Aug 17 2026

Today-Tonight... Broad upper level high pressure across the southern 
US and Florida will remain in place through the day. At the surface, 
high pressure across the Gulf will remain in place with the Atlantic 
ridge axis drifting southwards as a weakening frontal boundary 
shifts southward across the southeastern US. Locally, offshore flow 
will persist, both at the surface and aloft, with flow remaining 
weak. The east coast sea breeze has formed this afternoon, mainly 
from Cape Canaveral southward, turning the winds south to 
southeasterly along the coast. The sea breeze is forecast to form 
north of Cape Canaveral as well later this afternoon, but is 
expected to remain fairly close to the coast. A pool of higher 
moisture (PW values of 2.0-2.3") will filter down across the 
northern part of the CWA head of the aforementioned frontal 
boundary, while drier air (PW values around 1.6-1.9") remains across 
the southern part of the warning area. This will result in better 
rain chances across the north, mainly from Kissimmee to Cape 
Canaveral northward, where rain chances are 20-50 percent this 
afternoon. Already this afternoon we have scattered showers and 
storms moving in from the west coast of Florida, and moving
across Lake County and into Volusia County. 

The environment will support convection this afternoon, with 
forecast soundings showing  plenty of instability (MUCAPE 2000-2500 
J/kg), ample buoyancy (Lifted Index of -5 to -7), and sufficient dry 
air aloft with downdraft potential (DCAPE 900-1300 J/kg). Main storm 
hazards today will be frequent lightning strikes, gusty winds up to 
55 mph, and locally heavy downpours. Storm motion will be to the 
east through the day, eventually moving offshore. Any lingering 
activity will dissipate or move offshore this evening, becoming dry 
overnight with light westerly flow returning across the area. 

Another hot and humid day today, with above normal temperatures 
forecast. Afternoon highs will climb into the mid to upper 90s 
across east central Florida this afternoon, which some locations 
will be near their daily record highs (see climate section below).
These hot temperatures combined with high humidity will produce 
peak heat indices of 108- 112F. A Heat Advisory remains in effect 
for all of east central Florida through 8 PM this evening. 
Adequate hydration and breaks in the shade or an air conditioned 
building will be crucial for those spending extended periods of 
time outdoors. Residents and visitors alike are encouraged to 
practice heat safety to help avoid developing heat illness. 
Temperatures overnight will remain warm and muggy, with overnight 
lows in the upper 70s to low 80s. 

Tuesday-Sunday... Upper level high pressure across the southern US 
will continue to broaden through the week. A trough around the Great 
Lakes region will slowly shift eastward towards New Brunswick by 
late week, deepening across the eastern US and expanding farther 
southward through the weekend with a series of shortwaves traversing 
the base of the trough. At the surface, high pressure in the central 
Gulf will slowly shift eastward through the week, with the Atlantic 
high remaining in place. Locally, the high pressure in the Gulf will 
maintain persistent offshore flow through the period. The east coast 
sea breeze is forecast to form each day, turning the winds onshore 
along the coast. Moisture will increase across the area this week, 
with forecast PW values ranging from 1.7-2.3". This will allow a 
return of dirunally-driven showers and lightning storms each day 
through the time period. Rain chances will become near normal for 
this time of year, with PoPs ranging between 40-60 percent each 
afternoon, with the sea breeze collision favoring the eastern side 
of the peninsula each day. Showers and storms will push offshore in 
the dominate westerly flow. Storms will be capable of producing 
frequent lightning, gusty winds of 40-50 mph, and locally heavy 
rainfall. Any lingering activity will push offshore or dissipate 
into each evening. 

Hot and humid conditions will persist through at least Wednesday, 
with temperatures forecast to trend slightly downwards late week and 
into the weekend due to the higher rain chances. Additional Heat 
Advisories for portions of ECFL may be needed, especially through 
mid week. Overnight lows will be seasonable to slightly above normal 
each night.
